scenarios.reason: The formulation stops at anything bought in finished. What it contains is what the supplier declares, recorded with who declared it and whether the organisation checked it.

scenarios.question: A supplier changes what is inside an ingredient. Which of our labels does that reach?
scenarios.reason: The supplier's change notice is a document dated after the formulation now in force, so the ingredient is found from the notice, every product using it is found through the composition, and each pack's printed items are recorded for each product.

scenarios.question: We reformulate to cut sugar by 30%. Which claims and labels does that reach?
scenarios.reason: The sugars value, the claims resting on sugars and the label items of the product are found directly, and so are the products that use it as an ingredient. Whether a claim still meets its condition after the change is judged by the person responsible, because the condition is held as wording.

scenarios.question: Which product's date mark is set by its shortest-lived ingredient?
scenarios.reason: The sources say a shelf life is limited by the shorter of a food's safe life and its quality life. None says an ingredient's own life sets the product's, so the design keeps a shelf life for each product and does not work one out from its ingredients.

scenarios.question: Which batches contain the recalled ingredient?
scenarios.reason: Every product using the ingredient can be found through the formulation. Which batches of those products contain the affected material is a manufacturing question and out of scope.

standards_conformance.how_satisfied: All three domains are reused as DDA holds them, so nothing here is owned by a single department.
Each requirement names an accountable role, and what could not be checked is raised as an open decision or a finding rather than worked around.
Policy ownership. Nothing in this design changes who owns the policy.
Policy precedence. No conflict with a more specific policy arises in this design.
Policy scope. This design does not decide which data the policy applies to.
No new domain is proposed. Products was added to DDA as DMD000000032 and is reused as it stands.
Every domain is named for a subject. Six activity- or role-shaped candidates were tested and are recorded with the test each failed and where their subjects sit.
Stewardship and custodian roles are assigned outside a model design.
Each concept sits in exactly one domain and each domain has one anchor concept. Products had no concepts in DDA, so its anchor concept, Product, is proposed here.
Authoritative repositories are named per domain outside a model design.
Lineage is held by the platform and is not modelled.
Products carry an identifiers concept with the trade item number and internal numbers as further keys, each with its issuer and dates.
Attributes that carry a regulatory duty — allergens, nutrition basis, claim conditions, date marks, formulation versions and specification limits — are marked critical.
Issue management is a programme, not a model artefact.
Change control of the policy itself is outside a model design.

Each of the fourteen principles is addressed in turn. Three do not apply and one applies in part, because this design defines no reports, data products or publication. Three are not fully met and are set out as exceptions, each with its consequence and what would resolve it.

by_principle.1: A product is defined once, as the Product concept. What a product is to another party, such as an ingredient, a variant or a bought-in material, is a role that comes from a relationship, not a field on the product. Suppliers, certifying bodies and the business named on a pack are Legal Entities playing roles in the same way. One exception applies: some changes make a different product under an external identity rule (see below).
by_principle.2: The requirements in section 3 and the data requirements in section 4 set out the business meaning first, in business words, each with a source. The requirements draw on published sources alone (assumption SCA004). No tool, pipeline or physical structure is chosen.
by_principle.3: The design starts from {sources} published sources, listed in Appendix A with the reason each is included. It brings in no source data. A supplier's statements are kept with who made them and whether the organisation checked them.
by_principle.4: A product is identified by the identifiers it carries, such as a trade item number, an internal material number or a supplier's part number, each with its issuer and dates. Suppliers and documents use the identity DDA already has. Nothing depends on a report or a data product.
by_principle.5: Does not apply. This design defines no reports.
by_principle.6: Applies in part. The product definition is written once so that other models can refer to it (section 5.2). No data product is designed here.
by_principle.7: There are nine relationships (section 5.4). Each has a verb that reads naturally in both directions, the role at each end, how many can link, and whether dates are kept. None is reduced to a field on either side.
by_principle.8: The list of changes to make in DDA is generated from the model ({operations} steps in dependency order), and this document is produced from the same working files. One exception applies: DDA's Products definition disagrees with a requirement (see below).
by_principle.9: Definitions are written in the business's own words. Each concept shows a plain name beside its DDA name, and the requirements use the vocabulary of the field.
by_principle.10: No concept, list of values or relationship refers to an application, a report or a project.
by_principle.11: Does not apply. This design defines no data products.
by_principle.12: Does not apply. This design defines no publication of information.
by_principle.13: Sensitivity is set on {classified} of the facts the design keeps, where it applies, and {critical} are marked critical because they support a legal or safety duty. Retention and provenance are looked after by the platform and are not modelled here. Stewardship and retention are not defined, which is an exception (see below).
by_principle.14: The model uses the things the business itself talks about, products, ingredients, suppliers and certificates, and the arrangements between them, as the requirements describe them.

standards_conformance.how_satisfied: The glossary standards define domain, model, concept, attribute, producer, consumer, custodian, operational data store, master data management, warehouse, lake and critical data element. The design uses each term as defined.

exceptions.justification: An external identity rule makes a change to the declared ingredients, the net quantity, a certification mark or the pack count a different product (requirement REQ009). Principle 1 asks that identity survive changes over time. For these changes it does not. In this conflict the design follows the requirement.
exceptions.consequence: A question about one product over time has to follow a link from the old product to the new one, and cannot rely on a single identity. Anyone counting products before and after such a change will count two.
exceptions.route_back: Restating REQ009 so that such a change is a new version keeps one identity. The identity-changes concept would then be replaced by formulation versions.

exceptions.justification: DDA's Products definition says each product points up to one immediate parent product. Requirement REQ005 says the same ingredient goes into many products, so a product can have many parents and the composition relationship is many to many. In this conflict the design follows the requirement.
exceptions.consequence: If the DDA definition is followed as written, an ingredient could be recorded under only one product. The DDA definition and this design disagree, and an implementation generated from the definition would not meet the requirement.
exceptions.route_back: Rewording the Products definition in DDA so that a product may be used in more than one product removes the conflict. Keeping the wording means restating REQ005 and changing the composition relationship.

exceptions.justification: Principle 13 asks for stewardship, retention and provenance to be defined as part of the design. This design names no steward for any concept, sets no retention period for the dated history it keeps, and leaves provenance to the platform.
exceptions.consequence: Nobody is named as accountable for the definition of a concept, list of values or relationship, and nothing says how long formulation, specification or declaration history is kept.
exceptions.route_back: Naming a steward for each domain and setting a retention period for the dated history resolves it.

summary:
This design covers what a food or beverage product is, what goes into it, what it must be, how long it lasts, who may supply its ingredients and what may be said about it on pack. The formulation, meaning the list of what goes into a product and how much, is at its heart. The order ingredients are listed in, the allergens, the nutrition values and the claims on a pack all follow from the formulation, so a change to it shows which labels and claims it reaches. Where an ingredient is bought in already made, the design relies on what the supplier declares is inside it, and records who declared it and whether it was checked.

The design has three stated limits. It cannot say what is inside a bought-in ingredient beyond what the supplier declares. It finds every product that uses a recalled ingredient but not which batches, which belongs to the manufacturing model. It keeps a shelf life for each product and does not work one out from the shelf lives of its ingredients, because none of the sources describe a rule for doing so.

withdrawn_decisions.withdrawn_reason: Settled: the design holds a universal list of allergen foods and a list for each market, each market allergen naming the food it is.
